# Toy Production Function

## In plain English

A production function says how much a worker can make with a given amount of equipment. Give a baker one oven and they bake far more bread than by hand; give them a second oven and output rises again, but by less, because one person can only tend so many ovens at once. A tenth oven barely helps at all. The function captures exactly this pattern: more equipment always helps, but each extra piece helps a little less than the piece before it.

**Why it matters:** Diminishing returns are what make capital per worker settle down instead of growing forever.

## Definition

Output per worker is a concave function of capital per worker:

$$y = f(k) = Ak^{\alpha}$$

where $0 < \alpha < 1$ makes each extra unit of capital add less output.

## Notation

| Symbol | Meaning | Type | Typical value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | Output per worker | Endogenous | — |
| $k$ | Capital per worker | State variable | — |
| $A$ | Productivity | Parameter | 1 |
| $\alpha$ | Capital share: curvature of $f$ | Parameter in (0, 1) | 1/3 |
| $f(k) = Ak^{\alpha}$ | Output as a function of capital | Function | — |
